name: McGreer Camper Park
note: Private RV park on a working farm (cattle pens and grain bins beside the sites) on County Rd 8 at the I-80 Big Springs interchange, next to a Maverik. Hosts let you choose your site; storm shelter on site. CAMPER-REPORTED RATE: $40 a night in October 2026 (RV Life review); the park has no web page of its own, only a 'Coming Soon' placeholder (2026-11-05). --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Camper-reported: $40 a night for a full-hookup pull-through (RV Life reviews, October and August 2026; one August 2026 report says $43). The park posts no rate of its own.

name: Nine Eagles State Park
note: Wooded southern-Iowa park near Davis City with a 64-acre lake (rowboats and electric motors only). The modern campground is a set of long pull-throughs in a clearing in the woods, about 800 m from the lake; the non-electric campground is separate, and there are primitive equestrian and youth-group sites too. No daily Iowa park-entry fee. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Water and showers are off from mid-October and the dump station closes for the winter.
field_notes.Fees: Off-season (October 16 - April 30) / peak (May 1 - October 15) prices, sales tax included: non-electric $10 / $12; electric $18 / $22. Plus $4-5 a night on Memorial Day, July 4th and Labor Day weekends. Iowa DNR's camping rates (updated February 15, 2026), matched on its booking site, read 2026-10-12.
field_notes.Sites: 27 electric sites in the modern campground (32-85 ft, mostly 56-ft pull-throughs) and 20 non-electric sites (30-ft back-ins) in the separate non-electric campground. The 7 equestrian sites (54-60) and the youth-group site are not counted.

name: Red Haw State Park
note: Iowa state park on high cliff overlooking 72-acre Red Haw Lake.  Some sites wooded, some full sun; threaded potable spigot at dump station; roads and facilities are somewhat poorly maintained.  No daily park-entry fee in Iowa, camping fee only.  --AWH  51 public campsites (41 electric, 1 non-electric RV, 9 tent-only) since the campground reopened. 100% reservable on ReserveAmerica, bookable up to 10 pm on the day of arrival (ReserveAmerica and Iowa DNR, read 2026-10-20). --Claude

Booking: min stay 2 nights on weekends (May 1 to October 31 (Friday and Saturday)), 3 on holidays (Memorial Day and Labor Day weekends; July 4th when it falls on a Monday)

field_notes.Season: ReserveAmerica: reservations April 1 - November 30 ('Open through Mon Nov 30 2026'). The DNR page says the campground 'accepts reservation April - October and is closed November - March', so the two official pages disagree about November.
field_notes.Booking: ReserveAmerica, campsites up to 3 months ahead. The booking site says the campground 'is 100 percent reservable and accepts reservations April 1 - November 30 until 10:00 pm CST the day of arrival'; the DNR page says 'The campground is 100% reservable and a reservation is required.' Iowa's rule for a 100%-reservable campground: a Saturday alone (or Saturday/Sunday on a holiday weekend) can be booked once the cutoff for the Friday arrival has passed unreserved; a Friday night alone cannot.
field_notes.Fees: Off-season (October 16 - April 30) / peak (May 1 - October 15) prices, sales tax included: non-electric $10 / $14; electric $18 / $22. Plus $4-5 a night on Memorial Day, July 4th and Labor Day weekends. Iowa DNR's camping rates (updated February 15, 2026), matched on its booking site, read 2026-10-12.
field_notes.Sites: ReserveAmerica lists 52 campsites: 41 electric RV sites, 1 non-electric RV site, 9 tent-only sites, plus the host site and 3 shelters. Listed equipment lengths for RV sites 20-70 ft (most 55-60 ft); all listed driveways back-in.

name: Clay County Fairgrounds
note: Camping on about 15 acres of open, gridded fields at the Clay County Fairgrounds in Spencer, open to travelers outside fair time. Pay after arriving, by phone or at the Events Center office (weekdays). Open campfires prohibited. Run by the Clay County Fair Association. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Outside fair time: $20 per 24 hours without utilities, $35 with utilities, $50 with utilities and sewer; pay by phone or at the Events Center office. Clay County Fair, read 2026-11-03.

name: Lost Island - Huston Park
note: Palo Alto County Conservation Board campground in Lost Island - Huston Park, 3 mi north of Ruthven on the NE side of Lost Island Lake (1,200 acres). The full-hookup sites are lots 1, 2 and 17-24. The park has a swimming beach with dock, a boat ramp, fishing docks, hiking trails and the Lost Island Nature Center; extra vehicles park at the nature center lot. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Self-register: the envelope stub goes on the site's numbered post and payment is due within two hours of arrival. After 14 consecutive days campers must leave for 3 nights.
field_notes.Fees: Palo Alto County: $25 electric and water, $30 full hookup (lots 1, 2 and 17-24); dump station $3.

name: Monona County Fairgrounds
note: Grass RV sites on the northwest corner of the Monona County fairgrounds in Onawa, run by the Monona County Fair Association. Off-season camping only: fair week is not sold. Enter from 15th St; campers report you can bump the curb to make a site a pull-through. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: By request form: 'you will get a response back if we have availability'. Off-season camping is any date outside fair week (July 7-12 in 2026).
field_notes.Fees: Monona County Fair off-season camping: $25 a night, water and electric, no sewer.

name: Pierce Creek Recreation Area
note: Page County Conservation Board's North Campground at Pierce Creek Recreation Area (361 acres, a 30-acre lake, trails and public hunting), in woods off 140th St north of Essex, well away from the lake. A camping cabin can be reserved; the park's equestrian campground is a separate loop. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Electric and water sites $15 a night; the primitive sites (no pad listed) are $6.
field_notes.Sites: North Campground: 11 electric/water sites on 30-70 ft gravel pads (sites 1-4, 12-18) and 7 primitive sites (5-11). The equestrian-only campground on the west side of the park is separate.

name: Pottawattamie County Fairgrounds Campground
note: Campground at the Pottawattamie County Fairgrounds in Avoca, home of the Original Pottawattamie County Fair, just off I-80; campers choose a site and pay at the self-pay box (cash). CAMPER-REPORTED RATE: $25 a night (August 2026). --Claude

field_notes.Fees: CAMPER-REPORTED RATE (August 2026): $25 a night for a full-hookup site, paid in cash at the self-pay box; no operator page posts a rate.

name: Featherstone Memorial Park
note: Calhoun County Conservation Board park (51 acres) on the northwest shore of North Twin Lake near Manson, on the bike trail that circles the lake. The RV rows sit inland of the park's shore road, with a strip of lakeside cabins and trees between them and the water; sites A1-A30 at the south end are extended-stay. --Claude

field_notes.Season: The county says the campground closes December through April (water and electric off); campers staying then still pay the nightly fee.
field_notes.Booking: First come; pay on site at the envelope box by the entrance. After 14 days a camping unit must leave for at least 3 nights; the extended-stay sites A1-A30 are exempt.
field_notes.Fees: Calhoun County: sites 1-29 (water/electric), 30-43 (full hookup) and extended-stay A1-A30 (water/electric) all $25 a night; primitive tent sites T1-T20 $15. Pay on site (envelopes and pay box at the entrance). Read 2026-11-03.

name: Prairie Bridges Park
note: City of Ackley park (101 acres of woods and prairie, six fishing ponds, three miles of trails, disc golf), a quarter mile from downtown; the campground is in the south part of the park, mostly across a creek bridge. Monthly and seasonal stays are also sold. CAMPER-REPORTED RATE: $25 a night (June 2026). --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Call ahead to reserve a campsite: 641-485-1623.
field_notes.Fees: CAMPER-REPORTED RATE (June 2026): $25 a night, two RV Life camper reports; the City of Ackley has no page for the park and posts no rate (an undated heritage-area listing says $15 RV, $8 primitive).

name: North Woods Park
note: Bremer County Conservation park, 82 acres a mile north of Sumner beside the Wilson Grove Wildlife Area and the A.F. Miller bog preserve in the Little Wapsi floodplain. Lower electric sites plus upper gravel-pad sites with water. Two ponds in Wilson Grove are a short walk from the campground; trails, disc golf, playground, two shelters. Vehicle gate closed after Oct 31. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: First come, first served; call the county (319-882-4742) for availability.
field_notes.Fees: Bremer County: lower electric (20/30 A) $20 a night, upper electric/water on gravel pads (20/30/50 A) $25, non-electric $15.

name: Coffins Grove Park
note: Delaware County Conservation Board park (22 acres of bur oak woods) 4 mi NW of Manchester on Early Stagecoach Rd. One gravel loop: the water/electric sites in a row along the east edge, electric-only sites inside the loop, primitive sites at its north end. Coffins Grove Creek runs through the woods north of the loop (stream fishing); the county warns it can flood into the park. Two picnic shelters, ball diamond, playground. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Delaware County campgrounds are usually open mid-April through mid-October; vehicle access is closed in late fall and winter.
field_notes.Booking: First come, first served; self-register within 1 hour of arrival. No camping unit may occupy a site more than 14 days out of any 19. Check-out 4 pm.
field_notes.Fees: Delaware County campsite map (dated 2/7/2024): A sites electric and water $25 a night, B sites electric only $20, C sites primitive $15, all per night per unit; self-registration within 1 hour of placing the camping unit; fees non-refundable. Read 2026-11-03.
field_notes.Sites: The county's 2024 campsite map shows 14 sites: 5 water and electric (6A-10A, a row along the east edge), 5 electric only (1B-5B) and 4 primitive (11C-14C, along the north end of the loop). The MyCountyParks page still says 18 (15 water and electric, 3 primitive).

name: Prairie Ridge Camping
note: Small family-owned park in open country a mile south of US 34 near Murray. The pull-through pads sit in a gravel fan beside the office, about 60-150 m from a small fishing lake (electric motors only) with a beach, water slide, docks and paddle-boat rentals; also a golf driving range, a tent area, a waterfront rental camper and a cabin. Buddy sites: 1-2, 3-7, 4-5. Come in from US 34 on paved R15: an RV Life camper (9/2026) warns that a route from the south via Grand River runs about 5 miles on dirt. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Call ahead or book on the park's website; pay on arrival and check in at the office before going to the site; check-in 2 pm.
field_notes.Fees: RV sites $40 a night ($240 a week, $650 a month plus utilities); a 4% fee on card payments. The rate page carries no date; RV Life campers paid $40-41 in May and September 2026.
field_notes.Sites: Ten full-hookup sites (1-4, 7-12) and two water-and-electric (5, 6); sites 1, 2 and 4 are metered for extended stays.

name: Big Foot Beach State Park
note: ~100-site campground; the upper loop is drive-in RV (gravel pads) with 34 electric sites, remainder non-electric; lower sites are walk-to tent. No water/sewer hookups; dump station, showers. Reservable online. Open seasonally ~late April-mid-October. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Approximate: About late April to mid-October.
field_notes.Fees: Base nightly fee (before any nonresident surcharge) for RV-capable sites (52 sites, 2 fee schedules), Tuesday nights 2027-05-11 and 2027-06-15, from the wisconsin.goingtocamp.com site fee panel.

name: Pike Lake Campground - Kettle Moraine State Forest (Pike Lake Unit)
note: Sunrise family campground in Kettle Moraine SF Pike Lake Unit; 32 sites (24 wooded, 8 open), 11 with electric. Open early April to third weekend of October. Reservable online. The 3 backpack sites are a separate hike-in area. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Approximate: Early April to the third weekend of October.
field_notes.Fees: Base nightly fee (before any nonresident surcharge) for RV-capable sites (32 sites, 2 fee schedules), Tuesday nights 2027-05-11 and 2027-06-15, from the wisconsin.goingtocamp.com site fee panel.

name: Minong Wild River Trail Campground
note: MUNICIPAL - Village of Minong RV park (reservations via Washburn County Parks), not private. 20 full-hookup (W/E/S) RV sites + 5 tent sites; built 2013, expanded 2025; ATV loading ramp, coin showers, flush toilets, dump, pavilion. Open May 1-Oct 15. Reservable online (7-day-advance + 2-night minimum). --Claude  MINIMUM STAY: 2 nights on reservations May 1 - Oct 16, 3 on holiday weekends; unreserved sites are first-come inside 7 days (Washburn County Parks, 2026-10-12). --Claude

Booking: min stay 2 nights (May 1 - Oct 16), 3 on holidays

field_notes.Booking: Reservations need 2 nights from May 1 to Oct 16, 3 on holiday weekends, and close 7 days ahead; inside 7 days unreserved sites are first-come (Washburn County Parks reservation rules).
field_notes.Fees: Village of Minong: 20 full-hookup RV sites $45 a night, tents $20. Read 2026-10-15.

name: Deep Lake Campground
note: On Deep Lake (no-wake); RV sites, cabins, tent sites, plus year-round mobile-home spots. Open ~Apr 15/May 1-Oct 15/31. Daily bookable online; seasonal by phone. Leans seasonal but daily availability exists. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Approximate: About April 15 or May 1 to October 15 or 31.
field_notes.Fees: Deep Lake: nightly rates from $45; season May 1 - Oct 31. Read 2026-10-15.

name: Petenwell County Park
note: Adams County park (2nd-largest county park in WI) on Lake Petenwell, 2004 Bighorn Dr, Arkdale. Large campground with electric and premium/lakefront sites, many with water hookup; heated showers, dump station, swimming area, boat launch, harbor slips. Reservable online or by phone; 2-night min; open year-round. --Claude  MINIMUM STAY: 2 nights on reservations; unreserved sites are first-come (Adams County Parks, 2026-10-12). --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Reservations need 2 nights; unreserved open sites are first-come (Adams County Parks).
field_notes.Fees: Adams County 2026: camper/RV $25 a night, premium/lakefront $30, including 2 car passes. Read 2026-10-15.

name: Coon Fork Lake County Park
note: Eau Claire County Parks & Forest, on Coon Fork Lake 4 mi E of Augusta (E25501 County Rd CF). 108 sites total incl. 39 electric (30/50-amp) in A and D loops; flush toilets, hot showers, dump, two beaches, non-motorized boat landing, lakeside sites. Season May 1-Sep 15 reservable online (peak), FCFS self-register off-season. Office phone (715) 839-4783. (RV Life unrated) --Claude

field_notes.Fees: 2026 season (May 1-Sep 15): basic $25, lakeside $27, electric $29, D-loop water+electric $34. Off-season FCFS self-register: $12 non-electric, $20 electric.

name: Dorchester City Park
note: Village of Dorchester ~40-acre park off County Rd A & Park St. ~30-40 sites incl. full-hookup 50-amp pull-throughs plus W/E and primitive. On-site stocked fishing pond. Call camping contact. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: City of Dorchester: water and electric $22 a night, full-hookup 50-amp pull-throughs $25; tents $12. Read 2026-10-15.

name: Hattie Sherwood Campground
note: City of Green Lake campground on the north shore of Green Lake, with a boat launch; Hattie Sherwood Beach is across the street.  RV sites in 20-, 30- and 50-amp tiers, plus tent sites with 20-amp power; drop-ins are taken when there is room. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Read on Campspot: one night for 2 adults, site rate before tax, every RV site type a 23-ft rig fits (20 Amp + Water, 20 Amp RV, 30 amp + Water RV, 30 amp RV, 50 amp + Water Premiere and 50 amp RV). October 2026: $38-47 on a Tuesday; $43-52 on a Saturday. June 2027 isn't open for booking yet. Plus the park's $3 'Booking Fee', once per stay on every type but 20 Amp + Water. The park adds 3% of the site charge as a 'Processing Fee' on every type but 20 Amp + Water. Campspot adds its own booking fee at checkout (3%, at least $3). Read 2026-10-13.

name: Pine Point County Park
note: Chippewa County Facilities & Parks campground on a peninsula in 3,900-acre Lake Holcombe (Holcombe Flowage), ~2.5 mi W of Cty M / Hwy 27, Holcombe. 48 wooded sites, all with 20/30/50-amp electric; many sites directly on the water with some offering boat docks ($5/night dock fee). Beach, swim area, playground, pavilion. Open ~first week of May through last week of October; reservable online May-mid-Sept, FCFS self-registration mid-Sept-Oct. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Approximate: About the first week of May to the last week of October.
field_notes.Fees: Chippewa County: sites $20 a night plus $7 for 20/30/50-amp electricity. Read 2026-10-15.

name: North Bay Shore County Park
note: Oconto County park (RV Life mis-tagged commercial) on the W shore of Green Bay N of Oconto (addr 500 Bay Rd). 34 daily sites + group site; ~6 paved, rest grassy/gravel, all level. Reservable online (2-night min). --Claude  MINIMUM STAY: 2 nights on reservations, 3 on holiday weekends; open sites can be self-registered at the campground (Oconto County parks page, 2026-10-12). --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Reservations need 2 nights (3 on holiday weekends), up to 14, and close 2 days before arrival; an open site can be self-registered at the campground (Oconto County parks page).

name: Stockholm Village Park Campground
note: Village of Stockholm park campground on Lake Pepin (Mississippi River). 23 sites with 50-amp electric (count reduced during high water); no water hookup at sites (potable water on-site, arrive with tank filled). Privy toilets, swimming beach, boat ramp, 700' fishing pier. Open seasonally ~April-Oct (April limited by flood risk). Fee envelope/drop box at entrance. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Approximate: Open April to October (April limited by flood risk).
field_notes.Fees: Village of Stockholm: RV camping with electricity $27 a night, $150 a week; tents $20. Read 2026-10-15.

name: Vernon County Fairgrounds Campground
note: Vernon County Fair Association campground at the county fairgrounds, Viroqua; 56 electric sites (50-amp available), two shower buildings. Open ~May-October except the week of the Vernon County Fair. Contact office; flat grassy fairground sites fit large RVs. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Approximate: Open May to October, except the week of the county fair.
field_notes.Fees: Vernon County Fair: camper and RV $30 a day, tents $15. Read 2026-10-15.
